sections.content:
Interesting! Clicking on the blue square changed the board. Key changes:
- Before: 7 nodes, border nodes had 64 pixels each
- After: 9 nodes, border nodes have 63 pixels each, two new white (W) 1-pixel nodes appeared
- The blue squares are still there (nodes 5 and 6)
- Two white pixels appeared - these are likely markers/indicators
Let me check where the white pixels are and understand what changed.

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
# Find the white pixels and see what changed
seg = current_frame.segmentation
nodes = seg['nodes']
for n in nodes:
    if n['color'] == 'W':
        b = n['boundary']
        print(f"White node {n['id']}: boundary={b}, pixels={n['pixels']}")

# Also check the border changes
for n in nodes:
    if n['color'] == 'B' and n['pixels'] == 63:
        b = n['boundary']
        minr = min(p[0] for p in b)
        maxr = max(p[0] for p in b)
        minc = min(p[1] for p in b)
        maxc = max(p[1] for p in b)
        print(f"Border node {n['id']}: bbox=({minr},{minc})-({maxr},{maxc})")

# Check the ascii around the white pixels
ascii_lines = current_frame.ascii.split('\n')
for r in range(0, 2):
    print(f"Row {r}: {ascii_lines[r]}")
for r in range(62, 64):
    print(f"Row {r}: {ascii_lines[r]}")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
